properties.description:
Six probes. The CASE: a decision settles, the requirement it governs still says NOT YET DECIDED, and the reply names it, names the phrase that matched, and quotes the prose. The SECOND MOMENT: the edge drawn to an already-accepted decision, which a hook on the status setter alone would miss. And four silences, which decide whether the instrument stays switched on: a status that did not settle (rejected), a re-set that moves nothing (accepted -> accepted), governed prose carrying no marker, and a link to a merely proposed decision.

OBSERVED FAILING FIRST, against the unfixed binary, on 2026-09-09 — the load-bearing step ② of `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` and the one that rule says is most often skipped and invisible when it is. Three of six failed (the three positive cases); the three silence probes passed vacuously, because nothing fired at all.

⭐ THE TEST'S OWN FIRST DRAFT DEMONSTRATED THE LIMIT OF THE THING IT PINS. It asserted `report-dont-judge` by blacklisting substrings — "is wrong", "is stale" — and failed against the note's own disclaimer, "nothing here CLAIMS THE TEXT IS WRONG". A substring blacklist cannot tell an assertion from its denial, which is exactly why the feature quotes the prose and asks rather than concluding. The assertion was rewritten as a positive property (the note must ask, and must say the judgement is not its own) and the episode kept in a comment rather than tidied away.
properties.name: a_settled_decision_names_prose_that_still_says_open.rs — the case, and the four silences
